messages:

Subject: Partnership: reseller model and lead registration questions

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Ridgeway is excited about a tighter partnership. Before we proceed with a term sheet, can you confirm a few things about Redwood's reseller program: 1) how commissions are calculated for deals that include both hosted subscription and professional services, 2) the lead registration window and what proof we need to register a lead, and 3) whether Redwood holds any portion of commission in escrow for chargebacks/early churn.

We have a handful of target accounts and want to make sure we register them correctly to avoid disputes. If you have a sample term sheet or registration template, please send.

Best,
Tom
---
Ridgeway Systems | Partnerships
Tom Reynolds | Head of Alliances
Tom: +1 (415) 555-0132

Hi Tom — great speaking with you. High-level answers below and I've attached a draft term sheet for Ridgeway (term_sheet_ridgeway_v1.pdf) plus a simple CSV template for lead registration. A few bullets to call out: 

- Commission structure (proposed): 20% of net subscription ARR on first year of customer billing; additional 10% commission for upsell revenue that originates from Ridgeway within 12 months of the first invoice; 5% recurring tail on renewals through month 36 for customers you originated.
- Multi-product splits: we allocate commission proportionally by billed revenue line items on the invoice (hosted subscription vs services). If integration services are contracted directly by Ridgeway (invoiced by you), Redwood pays only on Redwood-billed product revenue.
- Lead registration: register via the partner portal or the attached CSV within 30 days of first customer contact; include company domain, contact email, date of intro, and a short note on opportunity. We credit the registration after validation by Sales Ops (usually 48–72 hrs).
- Escrow/holdback: we typically hold 10% of the initial commission for 60 days to cover chargebacks and early cancellations. If the customer cancels within the holdback window, we will claw back proportionally.
- Onboarding credit: Ridgeway will receive a $2k onboarding credit applied to the first invoice after customer goes live.

Next steps: if this looks reasonable I can loop Legal and Finance to convert term_sheet_ridgeway_v1.pdf into a signable term sheet and adjust the holdback if you have concerns. I can also create the HubSpot deal (HSP-7892) and give you partner portal access.

Attached: term_sheet_ridgeway_v1.pdf; lead_registration_template.csv

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Quick clarifications from Sales Ops: 

- Exclusivity: default is non-exclusive. Any market exclusivity requests need additional approval and typically require revenue thresholds.
- Lead proof: CSV plus an initial intro email (forwardable) is required. For portal registrations the system timestamps the record.
- Registration fields: please include estimated ACV and expected close month; our ops team will add the deal to the partner pipeline once validated.

I'll attach the operational lead CSV (lead_registration_template.csv) and will prep the registration instructions doc if you want step-by-step.

-ben
Ben Carter | Sales Operations
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@ridgeway.ai>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks, Olga — that mostly works. Two asks from Ridgeway leadership before we sign: 

1) Can Redwood reduce the holdback from 10% to 5%? Our finance team flags 10% as a pretty sizeable cash timing impact for early-stage partners. If we accept 5% we can agree to the 60-day window.

2) On multi-product deals: in a recent engagement we expect Redwood subscription to be ~60% of invoice and Ridgeway-managed integration services ~40% (invoiced by Ridgeway). We want a clear, predictable rule that the commission paid by Redwood on mixed invoices is based only on Redwood-billed line items, and that the splits are documented on the invoice so the partner commission is straightforward.

Also — can you confirm whether onboarding credits apply to the first invoice regardless of whether Redwood or Ridgeway invoices the customer? That affects how we structure the first-month billing.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. If we can get to agreement, we'll have legal counters on the term sheet and then get the first set of registrations in this week.

—Tom
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@ridgeway.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-09T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partnership: reseller model and lead registration questions

Tom — appreciate the candor. We can accept reducing the commission holdback to 5% (subject to final Legal language) and retain the 60-day validation window. Confirming the multi-product rule: Redwood will pay commission on Redwood-billed revenue only; the allocation is proportional to the invoice line items when Redwood and Ridgeway both appear on a consolidated invoice. If Ridgeway invoices services directly, Redwood pays commission only on Redwood lines. We'll add explicit invoice-line documentation language to the term sheet.

Onboarding credit: applies to the first invoice that contains Redwood-billed product charges. If Ridgeway invoices the customer for the integration and Redwood bills later, the onboarding credit will apply on the first Redwood invoice (we will route credit via partner payout reconciliation). We'll document both flows in the SOW appendix.

Next steps: 
- I'll send term_sheet_ridgeway_v2.pdf with the adjusted 5% holdback and invoice-line language for signatures.
- Legal will prepare a short MOU + SOW appendix for onboarding credits and invoice mapping.
- Ben will create HSP-7892 and share partner portal access.
- Schedule a 30-min technical/ops handoff next week (I propose Aug 12 at 10:00 PT).

If that timeline works, we'll also ask you to upload initial lead registrations via the CSV by EOD Aug 11 so we can validate and lock credits.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
